title: Enough for today
thought: You don't need to fix your whole life today. Start with one thing.
action: Work on the thing you've been avoiding for 5 minutes.
question: What is one thing you've been avoiding because it feels too big?

title: Start before ready
thought: Waiting to feel ready is often just waiting.
action: Open the task and do the first visible step only.
question: What is the smallest next step you can see without planning the whole project?

title: Close one door
thought: Focus is less about willpower and more about fewer exits.
action: Put your phone in another room for one short work block.
question: Which distraction is easiest to remove for the next 25 minutes?

title: Show up small
thought: Consistency is built on returns, not perfect streaks.
action: Do today's version at half the size you planned.
question: What would "half size" look like for the habit you care about?

title: A quiet push
thought: Motivation fades. A finished first minute still counts.
action: Set a 5-minute timer and start before it ends.
question: If you only had five minutes, what would you choose to move?

title: Name the load
thought: Overwhelm shrinks when the next move has a name.
action: Write three tasks, circle one, ignore the rest for now.
question: Which one task would make the rest feel lighter?

title: Restart clean
thought: A missed day is information, not a verdict.
action: Do a two-minute restart of the habit you dropped.
question: What made it hard last time — and what is one easier setup?

title: A discipline window
thought: Discipline is often a protected window, not a personality.
action: Block 15 minutes on your calendar and keep only one task in it.
question: When today could that window realistically happen?

title: Evidence, not mood
thought: Confidence grows from kept promises to yourself.
action: Keep one small promise you can finish in under 10 minutes.
question: What promise is small enough that you can keep it today?

title: The first brick
thought: You don't need the whole staircase to place the first brick.
action: Define the outcome in one sentence, then start the first brick.
question: In one sentence, what does "done enough" look like?

title: A growth note
thought: Progress is easier to trust when you can point to it.
action: Write one sentence: what improved this week, even slightly.
question: What is one thing you handled better than last month?

title: After a miss
thought: Failure is a stop, not a identity. The next action is the exit.
action: Name the miss in one line, then take a 5-minute recovery step.
question: What recovery step would your future self thank you for?

title: Five-minute entry
thought: The hard part is usually entry, not the whole task.
action: Work for 5 minutes with permission to stop after.
question: What have you been negotiating with yourself about starting?

title: Clear one corner
thought: A fresh start can be physical: one clear surface, one clear task.
action: Clear one small surface or inbox row, then begin.
question: Which tiny mess is stealing the most attention?
